criteria.quote: Doduo flies poorly, but its heads steady its run.
criteria.revision: Replace the opening narration with: "Doduo’s two heads don’t just look unusual—they alternate to make its run more stable." This leads with the distinctive fact instead of restating the flight limitation.

criteria.quote: Its short wings make flying difficult, so it runs at high speed.
criteria.revision: Add a concrete physical detail after this line: "It can flee at over 60 miles per hour, leaving footprints up to four inches deep."

criteria.quote: If flying is difficult, why do Doduo’s heads alternate while it runs?
criteria.revision: Use this question only as the opening, without revealing the answer in the premise: "If flying is difficult, what are Doduo’s two heads doing during a sprint?" Delay the stability explanation until the later reveal.

criteria.quote: Short wings make flight difficult. This head rhythm supports high-speed running.
criteria.revision: Replace this repeated summary with an escalation based on the research: "Doduo can flee at over 60 miles per hour, and its powerful strides leave footprints up to four inches deep."

criteria.quote: At speed, Doduo raises one head while lowering the other.
criteria.revision: Move this reveal later and remove the same fact from the title and premise. Begin with Doduo’s difficult flight and fast running, then reveal: "Only during the sprint do we learn that one head rises as the other lowers."
Replace the fifth scene’s repeated flight-versus-running comparison with: "Its powerful strides can leave footprints up to four inches deep." This adds a new physical consequence of its running.

criteria.quote: Doduo’s short wings make flight difficult, while its alternating heads help stabilize high-speed running.
criteria.revision: End with a stronger evidence-based synthesis: "The answer is balance: Doduo alternates its heads to make running more stable, and those powerful strides can leave footprints up to four inches deep."

criteria.quote: Would you call it clever balance or strange design?
criteria.revision: Make the split more directly grounded in the evidence: "Is Doduo’s head rhythm a clever running advantage, or simply a response to wings that make flying difficult?"

findings.quote: Short wings make flight difficult. This head rhythm supports high-speed running.
findings.note: Scene "short-wings-running" repeats scene "running-instead". Replace it with a new step in the story.
